Methy]ene chloride is amongst the least toxic wldc]y used as an industrial solvent, particularly,

and hazardous of chlorinated in metal degreasing operations.

A prime requirement for any vapour degreasing solvent is its ability to dissolve all oils, waxes, resins, gums, etc, that are generally used in metal working operations. cleaning power is the greatest for methylene chloride.

greases, fats, The solvent

Vapour degreasing is a simple and effective process. When hot solvent vapours come into contact with a cooler object, they condense into liquid solvent on its surface, thereby, warming the This solution is then drained off. When the surface object and dissolving the greasy matter. condensation ceases and the clean, dry temperature of the object reaches that of the vapour, object can be removed from the degreaser. The solvent it and shall shall also clean the object without not reduce the gloss on the objectcorroding, oxidizing, staining, etching or fritting

Methylene chloride has low boiling point and is, therefore, also well suited for cleaning thermal switches, thermometers and other similar temperalure sensitive parts. It also has the highest solvent power and can remove tough paint residues and hard-to-dissolve resins effectively. The energy efficiency is also the highest with methylcne chloride. Tough least toxic of the chloromethanes, methylene chloride It is very dangerous to the eyes. dizziness and slight nausea. if sufficient precautions are taken ( see also Annex A ). is strongly narcotic and may cause It can, however, be handled safely,

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised)`. The off in accordance, number of significant places retained in the rounded off value, should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

ANNEX

A

HAZARDS

AND

SAFETY

PRECAUTIONS

FOR

METHYLENE

CHLORIDE

A-l Normally two types of hazards ar-e foreseen vapour inhalation and decomposition. A-2 The effect of inhaling solvent vapours at toxic levels can be acute or chronic or both. An acute, or one-time, high exposure can cause anesthetic effects, such as light headedness, dizziness, ioss of consciousness? or, if the exposure involves an excessively high concentration of solvent vapours, it can even cause death. Chronic exposure, under which a person continually and repeatedly inhales concentrated solvent vapours, can lead-to liver injury. A-2.1 Workers can be protoLted potential k.azards by observance set by various health agencies. from these of standards

A-3 Vapours of chlorinated solvents, even in relatively low concentrations, may decompose in contact with open flames or hot surfaces. In thermal decomposition, the chlorinated solvents breakdown to form hydrogen ch!oride, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide and phosgene. Should this happen, it will require unprotected workers to leave the area quickly, before other hazards ar-ise. A-3.1 For safety, chlorinated solvent vapours should be vented in order to avoid heat sources. Any welding operations should be stopped immediately, if the odour of chlorine 0r hydrogen chloride is noticed.

ANNEX

F

( Clause 5 )
SAMPLING OF METHYLENE OF CHLORIDE FOR ELECTROPLATING

F-l GENERAL REQUIREMENTS SAMPLING

F-l.1 Samples shall be taken in a protected place not exposed to damp air, dust or soot. F-l.2 The sampling and dry. instrument shall be clean

F-l.7 Each sample container shall be sealed air-tight after filling, and marked with full details of sampling, the date of sampling and details given under 3.2. F-2 SCALE OF SAMPLING F-2.1 Lot All the containers in a single consignment of the material of the same grade drawn from a single batch of manufacture shall constitute a lot. If a consignment is declared to consist of different batches of manufacture, the batches shall be marked separately and the groups of containers in each batch shall constitute separate lots. F-2.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the material in any lot to the requirements of this specification, samples shalI be tested for each lot separately. F-2.3 The number of containers to bc selected from the lot shall depend on lhe size of the lot and shall be in accordance with Table 2. 5

F-l.3 Precautions shall be taken to protect the samples, the material being sampled, the sampling instrument and the containers for samples from adventitious contamination. F-l.4 To draw a representative sample, the contents of each container selected for sampling shall be mixed as thoroughly as possible by suitable means. F-l.5 The samples shall be placed in suitable, clean, dry and air-tight glass bottles or other suitable containers on which the material has no action. F-l.6 The sample containers shall be of such a size that they are almost three-fourth filled by the sample.

IS 13443 : 1992 Table 2 Number of Containers to be Selected from Lots of Different Sizes ( Chuse F-2.3 )
Lot Size N (1) 3to 15 16 ,, 40 41 ,, 110 111 ), 180 181 ,, 300 301 ,, 500 501 ,, 800 801 and above Sample Size tl (2) 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 10

the lot size and sample size, respectively. Every rth container thus counted shall be withdrawn to constitute the sample. F-3 INDIVIDUAL SAMPLES COMPOSITE SAMPLE AND

F-3.1 From each of the containers selected according to F-2.3, a representative portion of the material, about 300 ml in volume, shall be drawn. From each of these individual portions, an equal quantity of the material shall be taken and thoroughly mixed to constitute a composite sample not less than 1 000 ml in volume. The composite sample shall be transferred to clean bottles and labelled with full identification particulars of the sample. F-4 NUMBER OF TESTS

F-2.3.1 These containers shal1 be selected at random. In order to ensure the randomness of selection, random number tables may be used ( see IS 4905 : 1968 ). In case the random number tables are not available, the following procedure may be used. Arrange all the containers in the lot in a systematic manner and starting from any one, count them as 1, 2 ,......... up to r where Y is the integral part of N/n; N and n being

F-4.1 Tests for the determination of the characteristics given in Table 1 shall be carried out on the composite sample. F-5 CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY

F-5.1 For declaring the conformity of the lot to the requirements of all the characteristics, the test results on the composite sample shall, meet the corresponding requirement specified.

Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BI or conformrty to that standard as a further safeguard.
